items.title: Relative finite presentation of a module is independent of the presentation and passes to finitely presented quotients of the algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A and an A-module M, and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that for some presentation alpha : R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A the module M be finitely presented over R[x_1, ..., x_n]; that the same hold for all presentations; and that for any surjection A' -> A with A' a finitely presented R-algebra, M be finitely presented as an A'-module; it adds that in this case M is a finitely presented A-module (source lines 20922-20936). The proof of the first equivalence is a comparison of presentations: given alpha and beta, the proof chooses f_j and g_i realising the two compositions and assembles the displayed commutative diagram, after which the equivalence of (1) and (2) follows from the finitely-presented-over-a-subring and finite-finitely-presented-extension lemmas (proof lines 20938-20954). The third condition is then related to the second in the substantive step: choosing a presentation A' = R[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f_1, ..., f_m), the proof uses the finite-finitely-presented-extension lemma again to show that M is finitely presented as an A'-module exactly when it is finitely presented as an R[x_1, ..., x_n]-module (proof lines 20955-20959), which gives the equivalence of (2) and (3). The non-routine content is the uniform use of the finite-extension criterion to relate the module-theoretic conditions across the two presentations and across the surjection A' -> A.
